plan.title: Mouse liver HFD vs chow DE + Hallmark pathways
plan.analytical_narrative: Raw Salmon gene-level counts (12000 genes x 12 mouse liver samples, 6 high-fat diet vs 6 chow, unpaired, single batch) are first checked for sample structure with a blinded VST/PCA/sample-distance QC that explicitly inspects sample_01 (library size ~4x below median) rather than silently dropping it. DESeq2 then models raw counts with a minimal low-count pre-filter, median-of-ratios normalization built into the model, an explicit condition factor (reference level = chow) and a Wald test for the HFD-vs-chow contrast, with apeglm shrinkage of the reported fold change and BH-adjusted independent filtering at alpha 0.05. The DESeq2 Wald statistic ranks the full gene list (no pre-filtering by significance) for a preranked fgsea analysis against the MSigDB mouse Hallmark collection staged in this environment (mh.all.v2026.1.Mm.symbols.gmt, MGI symbols, native mouse annotation, no ortholog mapping needed). A final report step consolidates DE tables, fit diagnostics, the leading-edge genes of significant pathways, and a full reproducibility record, explicitly flagging the low-depth sample and the disputed enrichment ranking-metric choice (Wald stat) per the sourced procedure.
